title: Car Loan Interest Tax Deduction Calculator 2026 (OBBBA)
description: Estimate your 2026 OBBBA car loan interest deduction: up to $10,000 of interest on a new, U.S.-assembled personal-use vehicle, with the $100k/$200k MAGI phase-out and your federal income tax savings.
answerSnippet: The 2026 OBBBA car loan interest deduction lets you deduct up to $10,000 of interest on a new, U.S.-assembled personal-use vehicle bought after 2024. It phases out above $100,000 MAGI ($200,000 married) and is available even without itemizing.
intro:
For the first time in decades, **personal car loan interest** can be tax-deductible. The **One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA)** created a temporary deduction for tax years **2025 through 2028**: up to **$10,000** of interest per year on a loan for a **new, personal-use vehicle** with **final assembly in the United States**.

This is unusual — normally only **business** vehicle interest is deductible. And unlike itemized deductions, you can claim this one **even if you take the standard deduction**.

The rules are specific. The vehicle must be **new** (not used), for **personal use**, and the loan must be **secured by the vehicle** and **originated after December 31, 2024**. You report the **VIN** on your return. Enter the **interest you paid this year**, your **filing status**, and your **MAGI** to see your deduction and the federal tax it saves.
keyTakeaway: Deduct up to **$10,000** of interest on a **new, U.S.-assembled, personal-use** vehicle whose loan started **after Dec 31, 2024**. The deduction phases out **$200 per $1,000** of MAGI over **$100,000** (single) / **$200,000** (joint) and is gone at **$150,000 / $250,000**. Available with the standard deduction. Temporary: **2025–2028**.

explanation:
## How the car loan interest deduction works

```
Eligible interest = min(interest paid, $10,000)
Phase-out         = −$200 of deduction per $1,000 of MAGI over the threshold
Threshold         = $100,000 single / $200,000 married filing jointly
Tax saved         ≈ deduction × your marginal federal rate
```

The phase-out is **steeper** than the tips/overtime ones — **$200 per $1,000** (20% of the excess). A single filer at **$120,000** MAGI is $20,000 over the threshold, cutting the deduction by **$4,000**. It reaches **$0** at **$150,000** (single) / **$250,000** (joint).

## Which vehicles qualify

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Condition | **New** vehicle (not used) |
| Use | **Personal** use (not a business/fleet vehicle) |
| Assembly | **Final assembly in the United States** (check the VIN / window sticker) |
| Loan date | Loan **originated after December 31, 2024** |
| Security | Loan **secured by** the vehicle |
| Reporting | **VIN** reported on your tax return |

Refinancing a qualifying loan can still qualify, but only interest on the **original balance** counts — cash-out amounts above the original loan do not.

## Why it is notable

- It is available **without itemizing** — most taxpayers take the standard deduction and can still claim this.
- It does **not** apply to leases, used cars, or motorcycles/vehicles assembled outside the U.S.
- Interest above **$10,000** in a year is not deductible.

## Disclaimer

Educational estimate of a federal deduction. Savings depend on your full return and marginal rate; state tax and credits are not modeled. Confirm your vehicle's U.S. final assembly and your loan's eligibility with the IRS guidance and a tax professional before relying on the deduction.

faq.q: Can I deduct car loan interest in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, under a temporary OBBBA rule you can deduct up to **$10,000** of interest per year on a loan for a **new, personal-use vehicle** with **final assembly in the United States**, if the loan started **after December 31, 2024**. It applies to tax years 2025–2028.
No. The deduction only covers **new** vehicles. Used cars, leases, and vehicles assembled outside the U.S. do not qualify, and the loan must be **secured by** the vehicle.

faq.q: How do I know if my car was assembled in the U.S.?
faq.a: Check the **VIN** and the window sticker (Monroney label), which lists the final assembly point. You report the **VIN** on your tax return, and only vehicles with **U.S. final assembly** qualify.

faq.q: What is the income limit for the car loan deduction?
faq.a: It phases out when **MAGI** exceeds **$100,000** (single) or **$200,000** (married filing jointly), losing **$200 per $1,000** over the threshold. The deduction reaches **$0** at $150,000 (single) / $250,000 (joint).

faq.q: Do I have to itemize to claim it?
faq.a: No. This deduction is available **even if you take the standard deduction**, which makes it usable by most taxpayers who finance a qualifying new car.

faq.q: Does refinancing a car loan still qualify?
faq.a: Generally yes, if the original loan met the requirements. However, you can only deduct interest on the **original loan balance** — interest on any cash-out amount above that balance does not qualify.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how much interest I can deduct?
faq.a: Yes — **$10,000** of interest per year. Interest paid above that cap is not deductible, and the cap is the same for single and married filers.

faq.q: Which years does the deduction apply to?
faq.a: Tax years **2025 through 2028**. It is a temporary OBBBA provision and expires after 2028 unless Congress extends it.
